question: A certain amount grows to ₹6400 in 2 years and ₹7040 in 3 years at compound interest. Determine the interest rate.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For Compound Interest, the amount at the end of a year acts as the principal for the very next year.

Interest for the 3rd year = A₃ − A₂ = 7040 − 6400 = ₹640

Rate % = (Interest ÷ Principal) × 100

Rate % = (640 ÷ 6400) × 100 = 10%

**∴ The correct answer is 10%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Amount after 2 years (A₂) = ₹6400

Amount after 3 years (A₃) = ₹7040

*(Note: Based on the given options, the interest is compounded annually)*

**Formula Used:**

A = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ

 
• Year 0 Year 2 Year 3 Principal ₹6400 ₹7040 
• 
• 
• 
 + ₹640 (1 Year Interest) Rate = (640 ÷ 6400) × 100 = 10% 

**Calculations:**

⇒ For 2 years: 6400 = P(1 + R/100)² --- (Equation 1)

⇒ For 3 years: 7040 = P(1 + R/100)³ --- (Equation 2)

⇒ Dividing Equation 2 by Equation 1:

⇒ 7040 ÷ 6400 = [P(1 + R/100)³] ÷ [P(1 + R/100)²]

⇒ 704 ÷ 640 = 1 + R/100

⇒ 1.1 = 1 + R/100

⇒ R/100 = 0.1

⇒ R = 10%

**∴ The correct answer is 10%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Compound Interest Successive Years

The amount at the end of any year acts as the principal for the very next year. Rate = [(Aₙ − Aₙ₋₁) ÷ Aₙ₋₁] × 100.

Simple Interest vs Compound Interest

For the first year, SI and CI are identical. From the second year onwards, CI earns interest on the accumulated interest, whereas SI is always calculated on the initial principal only.

Difference Between CI and SI

For 2 years, Difference = P(R/100)². For 3 years, Difference = P(R/100)² × (3 + R/100).
